content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed a guide titled The WHO Application of ICD-10 to Deaths During Pregnancy, Childbirth, and the Puerperium: ICD-MM. This guide is based on the 10th revision of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems (ICD-10) and its coding rules. It aims to standardize the identification, reporting, and classification of maternal deaths to improve the accuracy and consistency of maternal mortality data. The guide was created to address the challenges in identifying and classifying maternal deaths, which often result in inconsistencies and misclassification. Maternal deaths are defined in the ICD-10 as those caused by direct or indirect obstetric causes, deaths during pregnancy, childbirth, and the puerperium, or late maternal deaths. Despite the existing ICD definitions, there is significant variability in how maternal deaths are reported and coded across countries, leading to underreporting and misclassification. The WHO guide provides a practical framework for healthcare providers, coders, epidemiologists, and researchers to accurately document and classify maternal deaths. It clarifies the application of ICD-10 codes, identifies conditions that may contribute to maternal deaths, and distinguishes between direct and indirect maternal deaths. The guide also includes appendices and tables to facilitate consistent reporting of clinical conditions and improve the attribution of causes of death. The development of this guide involved a consultative process with a technical working group comprising obstetricians, midwives, epidemiologists, and public health professionals from both developed and developing countries. The group adopted three key principles: the guide should be practical and user-friendly, the underlying cause categories should be mutually exclusive and clinically relevant, and the conditions should be grouped in a way that facilitates epidemiological analysis and health service planning. The guide was tested on maternal death data from various sources, including national registration and surveillance databases, health facility-based databases, and verbal autopsy data. Based on the feedback and experiences from these tests, the guide was revised and finalized to ensure its applicability and effectiveness. The ultimate goal of the WHO guide is to improve the quality and comparability of maternal mortality statistics, enhance the interpretation of data, and support the allocation of resources and programs aimed at reducing maternal mortality. By adopting the ICD-MM, countries can reduce errors in coding, improve the attribution of maternal deaths, and generate more reliable data for public health decision-making.
